## CL-02 Cleaning effectively

Status: applies
Reason:
Decided-by:
Variation:
Proved-safe:

### CL-02-Q01

> Cleaning and disinfection needs to be carried out in two stages:
>
> 1. Clean: Using either hot, soapy water or a cleaning product (such as a sanitiser), remove visible dirt, grease and debris from surfaces/equipment and wipe off or rinse.
> 2. Disinfect: Following the manufacturer’s instructions, apply a disinfectant (such as a sanitiser) all over the surfaces/equipment and leave on for the required contact time.
> Do you clean and disinfect using two stages?  (yes / no)
Answer:
State: unanswered
By:
On:
Source:

### CL-02-Q02

> Cleaning and disinfection needs to be carried out in two stages:
>
> 1. Clean: Using either hot, soapy water or a cleaning product (such as a sanitiser), remove visible dirt, grease and debris from surfaces/equipment and wipe off or rinse.
> 2. Disinfect: Following the manufacturer’s instructions, apply a disinfectant (such as a sanitiser) all over the surfaces/equipment and leave on for the required contact time.
> Have your staff been trained in how to complete the two stage clean?  (yes / no)

### CL-02-Q03

> Manufacturer’s instructions/BS EN standards:
> When using disinfectants or sanitisers, always follow the manufacturer’s instructions on the label. These instructions should tell you how to correctly dilute the product and how long you need to leave the product on the surface/equipment for harmful bacteria to be reduced to safe levels. Sanitisers and disinfectants should meet relevant standards, either BS EN 1276 or BS EN 13697.
> Where do you keep information to confirm your disinfectants or sanitisers meet BS EN 1276 or BS EN 13697 standards?  (write your answer)

### CL-02-Q06

> HIGH PRIORITY CLEANING
> Ideally use a dishwasher. Do not overload the dishwasher and make sure it is maintained and serviced regularly.
> If you do not have a dishwasher, wash plates, equipment, etc, in hot soapy water using bactericidal detergent.
> Ideally, separate sinks should be used for washing up equipment used for raw foods and equipment used for ready to eat foods.
> If you have to use the same sink, the water must be changed and the sink (including all taps/fittings) must be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected using a two stage clean between uses.
> Do you have a dishwasher?  (yes / no)
Answer:
State: unanswered
By:
On:
Source:

## CL-04 Your cleaning schedule

Status: adapted
Reason: Staff can see it and sign it where they work.
Decided-by: Sam Okafor
Variation: Our cleaning schedule is a laminated sheet on the kitchen wall that staff initial as each job is done, instead of the schedule pages in the pack.
Proved-safe: It lists the same things to clean, how often and who cleans them as the pack's schedule. The owner checks it every week and keeps each week's sheet.
